missions.profile: Wide-field infrared survey telescope with a Hubble-class mirror but a field of view roughly one hundred times larger, built to study dark energy and find exoplanets through microlensing and direct imaging.
NASA/ESA/CSA infrared flagship observing from Sun–Earth L2, covering everything from the first galaxies to exoplanet atmospheres.
The veteran NASA/ESA optical and ultraviolet observatory in low Earth orbit, still producing frontline science in its fourth decade.
NASA's programme to return astronauts to the Moon with commercial and international partners. Artemis I flew uncrewed in 2022; Artemis II is the first crewed flight.
Europa Clipper is en route to assess the habitability of Jupiter's moon Europa, arriving in 2030; ESA's JUICE mission follows to the icy moons in 2031.
Parker Solar Probe flies repeated record-close passes through the Sun's corona to trace how the solar wind is heated and accelerated.
NASA's surface fleet — the Perseverance and Curiosity rovers — continues exploring Jezero and Gale craters, with orbiters relaying data overhead.
Continuously crewed orbital laboratory operated with international partners, hosting rotating crews and microgravity research. Crew-13 took over in October 2026 after Crew-12 returned.
Joint ESA/JAXA mission carrying two orbiters to Mercury. After an eight-year cruise it is now in its arrival phase, ahead of orbit insertion.
ESA's Earth-watching fleet: the Copernicus Sentinels monitor land, ocean and atmosphere, now joined by Sentinel-3C and the FLEX Earth Explorer, which will map plant fluorescence globally.
missions.status: Operating; Sentinel-3C returned first images Oct 2026

missions.profile: Solar Orbiter studies the Sun at close range and from progressively tilted orbits, returning the first good views of the solar poles.
India's human spaceflight programme, working toward its first crewed orbital mission through uncrewed test flights and recovery testing.
Earth observation satellite providing imaging over the Indian region from geostationary orbit.
India's heaviest operational launch vehicle, used for Chandrayaan-3 and slated for Gaganyaan, powered by the CE20 cryogenic upper stage.
China's robotic lunar programme. Chang'e-6 returned the first far-side samples in 2024; Chang'e-7 and -8 target the lunar south pole ahead of a planned research station.
China's planetary exploration line: Tianwen-1 orbits Mars, Tianwen-2 is en route to sample the quasi-satellite Kamo'oalewa, and Tianwen-3 aims to return samples from Mars.
missions.expected: Tianwen-3 launch targeted 2028; Mars sample return around 2031

missions.profile: 8.4-metre survey telescope in Chile with the largest digital camera ever built, imaging the entire southern sky every few nights.
missions.expected: 10-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time

missions.profile: NASA's Earth-observing satellites, including the NASA/USGS Landsat series, track land, ice, ocean and atmosphere, with results published through NASA's Earth Observatory.
ESA's Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice) is cruising to Jupiter using a series of planetary gravity assists, to study Ganymede, Callisto and Europa from 2031.
missions.status: In transit; Earth flyby completed 28 Sep 2026

missions.profile: Mars Express, ESA's longest-serving Mars orbiter, images and maps the planet's surface, subsurface and atmosphere.
JAXA-led X-ray Imaging and Spectroscopy Mission, built with NASA, performing high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy of hot cosmic plasmas, from galaxy clusters to compact binary stars.
Compton Spectrometer and Imager, a NASA Small Explorer gamma-ray telescope being built at UC Berkeley to map how chemical elements form in the Milky Way.
NASA's flagship X-ray observatory, studying hot and energetic regions of the universe such as black holes, supernova remnants and galaxy clusters from a high elliptical Earth orbit.
China's modular space station in low Earth orbit, continuously crewed by rotating Shenzhou crews and preparing to host its first foreign astronaut from Pakistan.
Second-generation satellite for India's NavIC regional navigation system, part of the NVS series replacing the original IRNSS satellites.
Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging: a NASA Venus mission whose descent probe will study the planet's deep atmosphere.
Solar wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer, a joint ESA–Chinese Academy of Sciences mission imaging how Earth's magnetosphere responds to the solar wind.
PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics, a far-infrared observatory and the first mission in NASA’s new Probe Explorers class of astrophysics missions.
Thermal infraRed Imaging Satellite for High-resolution Natural resource Assessment, a joint ISRO–CNES mission to map land and water surface temperature for water-use and climate monitoring.

items.title: Crew-12 splashes down after 237 days on the ISS; ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot returns to Europe
items.summary: SpaceX Crew Dragon Freedom undocked on 7 October after a handover to Crew-13 and splashed down in the Pacific off California at 15:34 GMT on 8 October, carrying NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev. Adenot completed her εpsilon mission after 237 days and more than 3,700 orbits, and has since landed in Cologne, Germany.

items.title: Antarctic sea ice reaches its 2026 maximum, third-lowest on record
items.summary: Antarctic sea ice reached its annual maximum extent for 2026, the third-lowest maximum since satellite observations began.

items.title: Potentially habitable rocky exoplanet shows first signs of an atmosphere
items.summary: Astronomers report, for the first time, signs of an atmosphere on a potentially habitable rocky planet.

items.title: TRISHNA thermal-infrared satellite in advanced stage of development, ISRO says
items.summary: An ISRO official said the TRISHNA satellite is in an advanced stage of realisation.

items.title: China targets Mars sample return around 2031
items.summary: A Chinese scientist said China aims to return samples from Mars around 2031, through the Tianwen-3 mission.

items.title: Experimental heat-shield capsules tested on reentry of NG-24 cargo craft
items.summary: NASA tested next-generation heat-shield technologies for crews returning from the Moon and Mars by sending 12 small experimental capsules aboard Northrop Grumman's 24th cargo resupply spacecraft, which burned up on reentry after undocking from the ISS.

items.title: Chang'e-6 far-side samples contain a rare, highly magnetic form of iron
items.summary: Analysis of lunar far-side samples returned by China's Chang'e-6 mission found gamma iron, a rare and highly magnetic iron allotrope reported as never before found in natural lunar material.

items.title: Webb Picture of the Month shows gravitationally lensed galaxies multiplied like a house of mirrors
items.summary: A James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month shows background galaxies warped and multiplied into several images, in detail, by gravitational lensing.

items.title: Solar Orbiter flies through a solar-wind switchback and traces it to magnetic loops on the Sun
items.summary: ESA's Solar Orbiter passed through a switchback — a sharp kink in the magnetic field carried by the solar wind — and researchers traced its origin back to magnetic loops at the Sun's surface, shedding light on how these structures form.

items.title: Sentinel-2 images Etosha, Namibia's biggest salt pan
items.summary: This Copernicus Sentinel-2 image, acquired on 5 April 2026, shows Etosha National Park and its salt pan in northern Namibia.

items.title: Satellites track widespread flooding in Thailand
items.summary: NASA's Earth Observatory documented flooding across Thailand caused by heavy rains since mid-September, which has affected millions of people.

items.title: Sentinel-3C returns its first images of Earth
items.summary: Two weeks after launch, Copernicus Sentinel-3C returned its first images and measurements from two of its key instruments, confirming the satellite is working well as it prepares to monitor oceans, land, cryosphere and atmosphere.

items.title: ISRO launches EOS-05 Earth observation satellite
items.summary: ISRO successfully launched the EOS-05 Earth observation satellite.

items.title: NASA releases full Artemis II lunar science dataset and crew imagery
items.summary: NASA made the complete lunar science dataset from Artemis II's crewed flight around the Moon available to scientists and the public on 7 October, including the crew's imagery and observations. Released material includes annotated tablet screenshots, such as an April 6 visualization of the Moon eclipsing the Sun.

items.title: Mars Express study suggests exotic physics behind Arsia Mons' elongated cloud
items.summary: Scientists combining Mars Express observations with a state-of-the-art Martian meteorological model found that unusual physics may lie behind the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud, Mars's most curious cloud.

items.title: Curiosity looks back over Gale Crater after climbing 1 kilometre
items.summary: NASA's Curiosity rover captured a view back across the floor of Gale Crater, with the crater rim in the distance, on 5 September 2026 (sol 5,006). Nine days earlier, on sol 4,996, the rover reached the milestone of 1 kilometre of elevation gain.

items.title: Curiosity captures sunrise over wind-carved yardangs
items.summary: Curiosity photographed a panorama of dawn light on distant wind-carved features called yardangs on 11 August 2026 (sol 4,982); scientists aim to learn how the yardang layer formed.

items.title: NASA publishes artist’s concept of PRIMA far-infrared observatory
items.summary: NASA released an artist’s concept of the proposed design for the PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics (PRIMA), selected in September 2026 as the first mission in its new Probe Explorers class.

items.title: Archival Hubble data point to a suspected second-generation planet around a white dwarf
items.summary: Unidentified chemical signatures from the white dwarf HS 0209+0832, held in the Hubble archive for more than 25 years, were found to include high amounts of niobium and other unusual abundances. Astronomers suggest a second-generation planet orbiting the white dwarf as a possible explanation.

items.title: Juno reveals a rippling current sheet in Jupiter's magnetodisk driven by magnetic reconnection
items.summary: Data from NASA's Juno spacecraft show a rippling current sheet in Jupiter's magnetodisk generated by magnetic reconnection.

items.title: Webb images outflows from a nebula's stellar jets
items.summary: A new James Webb Space Telescope image released by ESA shows the turbulent activity created by stellar jets in a nebula.
